0.content:
Dvalin is the Anemo Dragon Sovereign and the Dragon of the East of the Four Winds, and Venti's friend for around two thousand years. A newborn dragon whose size caused accidental havoc, he was drawn by the music of the Holy Lyre der Himmel. Barbatos calmly sang of his beauty while people panicked, then taught him human speech and song and taught Mondstadt not to fear him. Five hundred years ago Barbatos called him to fight the black dragon Durin. Dvalin killed it but swallowed its poisoned blood and slept in Decarabian's ruined tower. When he woke, the people had forgotten him and the poison tormented him. The Abyss Order convinced him his god had abandoned him and drove him to attack Mondstadt as "Stormterror". Venti and the Traveler purified him. Afterward Venti refused to command him: "freedom, if demanded of you by an archon, is really no freedom at all."

Venti's ballads credit "the East Wind" with the harvests. Dvalin can still be summoned by Der Frühling: he flew the Traveler, Jean, Barbara and Klee to the Golden Apple Archipelago (1.6, limited event), and in 6.4 he carried the Traveler to Nod-Krai. He shuns crowds; the city is too small for his wings, and he turned down the banquet at the end of the 6.4 Homeward event (limited). Venti introduced the reborn Durin to him and reports that the old dragon was the more excited of the two.

In the 6.4 Homeward event (limited), a memory bubble replayed the crisis as if the Traveler had never come. That Dvalin was beyond saving and had to be killed, and Venti said quietly that he had been "prepared for that possibility back then, too". Varka observed that Dvalin is family to Barbatos.

1.content:
Barbatos and Morax are the last two of the original Seven and old friends of a lopsided kind. The first time Barbatos descended on Liyue, Morax assumed a crisis and prepared to help; Barbatos tossed him a bottle: "Here's some wine from Mondstadt. Care for a taste?" He kept visiting with endless questions, and the first Seven began gathering in Liyue. Venti tried forging Morax's seal as a prank and never fooled him, and gleefully quotes "epic poems of days gone by" calling the Geo Archon "a brutish blundering buffoon". Zhongli sniffs that the bard "reeks of wine" and is "a disgrace to the arts", yet still remembers how those wines tasted.

After Rex Lapis's staged death, Venti wanted to bring Zhongli a vintage dug up at Windrise as a "condolence gift", while nervously asking how strong the old block-head still seemed. During the 6.4 Homeward event (limited) he noted that Signora won the Geo Gnosis by contract, not force. At Liyue's Lantern Rite (3.4, limited event) the two recognised each other and agreed to pretend they had not.

key: the boy who wished to see birds
2.content:
In storm-walled Old Mondstadt the wind spirit befriended a boy who played the lyre, dreamed of writing the greatest poem and had never seen the sky: "I do so wish to see the birds in flight." The spirit fetched him an eagle's feather. The boy raised a rebellion against Decarabian and the spirit joined him. The tyrant fell, but the boy died before Venti could give him the feather. On ascending, Barbatos remade himself in the boy's likeness so he could play the lyre the boy loved, and founded a free Mondstadt believing the boy "would have wanted to live in such a place."

He rarely speaks of it. In his Story Quest he told the Traveler only that his form was "a friend's", like "Stanley" wearing his partner's name. The Traveler sent Paimon off for food so he would not have to say the rest, and Venti called them a true friend for it. He then sang the boy's song and sat in silence by the statue.

A 6.3 artifact text (A Note in Spring's Leich) adds that the boy, at the moment of the god's fall, played a melody belonging to the Master of Time. It turned the dying storm into a thousand-year song called Mondstadt, but his body could not bear it and his name was swept away by time. The wind spirit, granted Time's authority, silently claimed "a strand of time from bygone days" and "the name that even the reversal of years could not save". This strongly implies the boy's name was Venti.

3.comment: Venti: Signora and the Anemo Gnosis
3.content:
After Dvalin was saved, Signora, Eighth of the Fatui Harbingers, ambushed Venti outside the Favonius Cathedral. She froze him in place, called him Mondstadt's "rodent ruler" and slapped him when he talked back. Then she plunged her hand into his chest and pulled out the Anemo Gnosis, a chess-piece-like crystal, while her agents knocked out the Traveler. Venti recovered at the Windrise oak and explained to the Traveler what a Gnosis is: an Archon's internal focus that resonates with Celestia, unlike a mortal's Vision.

Signora later took the Geo Gnosis by contract and died in Inazuma. The Anemo Gnosis went to the Tsaritsa, who by 7.1 holds all but the lost Pyro Gnosis.

During the limited-time 6.4 Homeward event, Venti told Varka that the Gnosis "was of no use to me". He did not fight because the Cathedral, perhaps the whole city, would have become collateral damage. He thought Signora used force only because a newly woken god seemed no threat, and that her success led her to overreach against the Raiden Shogun.

4.content:
Venti met the Traveler in the Whispering Woods, when their sudden Anemo power broke his healing link with Dvalin. He soon realised their unique power could purify Dvalin's corrupted tears, and the two saved Mondstadt together. He calls them his muse, wants the world's bards to tell the Traveler's tales, and says wherever he roams, it must be with them. He named them the "Windborne Outlander". His parting advice, repeated years later, is that "the journey itself has meaning".

Paimon calls him the Tone-Deaf Bard and "Mr. Big Anemo God Barbatos"; he calls her a pesky little pixie, parrots her complaints and secretly enjoys her. When she asked (6.2) what other tricks he was hiding up his sleeve, he replied that he only had two sleeves.

In 6.2 he invited the Traveler to play a duet on the Nameless Island, "just a duet between friends". The last time he played that song, only the howling gale had listened.

5.comment: Venti: Holy Lyre der Himmel, Der Frühling and the fake Vision
5.content:
Archons do not need Visions, but Barbatos wanted to roam freely as Venti, so he made a glass ornament that looks like an Anemo Vision. It has no power, and he jokes he can make you a matching one. Too lazy to carry a lyre, he lets it turn into his wooden lyre, Der Frühling. His divine instrument, the Holy Lyre der Himmel, is a Church relic used at Ludi Harpastum. During the Stormterror crisis he asked Sister Gotelinde for it, introducing himself as Barbatos; she dismissed him as a bard full of nonsense. The Fatui stole it, Diluc's raid recovered it, and its strings were restored with purified tears, but it broke when an Abyss Mage intervened. Venti "repaired" it with an illusion just long enough to hand it to a horrified Barbara.

In game, the fake Vision does not react to meteor fragments or Starsplinter Iron the way real Visions do.

6.content:
Venti knew the Cryo Archon well five hundred years ago. After "a certain catastrophe" she cut off all ties with him, and he has not seen her since. He never imagined she would plot to steal another Archon's Gnosis, and he wonders what she is planning. His fabricated ballads have Barbatos pinching her scepter.

By 7.1 she holds six Gnoses; she collects them both to fight the Heavenly Principles and because a seal left by the Third Descender responds only to a Gnosis. Venti knows none of this first-hand. In the Snezhnaya Archon Quest (7.1) she told the Traveler that gods' love for humanity was imposed by the Heavenly Principles. The Traveler remembered Venti's words: "Freedom, if demanded of you by an archon, is really no freedom at all." In the 6.4 limited event he mused that he might formally meet her in Snezhnaya sooner than expected. As of 7.1 he has not.

7.comment: Venti: Decarabian and the Liberation of Old Mondstadt
7.content:
About 2,600 years ago Decarabian, God of Storms, ruled from a tower and walled his city in by gales so fierce that birds could not pass. His war with the wolf god Boreas buried the land in ice. The Gunnhildr Clan fled and prayed. The wind spirit heard them, sheltered them and gave their chieftain's daughter the power to protect. The rebellion that followed was led by the boy bard with the wind spirit, Amos (Decarabian's former lover), Gunnhildr and the Red-Haired Warrior. The tower fell; Decarabian died believing his people loved him. Barbatos then scattered the snow, split the mountains (some peaks still rise from the sea) and led the people to Cider Lake. As he explained during a limited-time Windblume event, "Windblume" began as a code word for staying in contact and resisting in secret. The ruins are today's Stormterror's Lair.

In the same event he told the Traveler that a Windblume is not one flower but whatever stands for each person's longing to be free. Boreas, seeing his own protection had been no different from the tyrant's tower, gave up his claim and left Mondstadt to the new god.

8.comment: Venti: Vennessa and the Forged Treaty
8.content:
A thousand years ago the Lawrence-led aristocracy ruled through slavery and pacts with monsters. The cries of the oppressed woke Barbatos. When the enslaved Vennessa was forced to fight Ursa the Drake, he appeared in divine form, lent her his power, and held Lord Lawrence to his promise to free her people. The soldiers turned on their masters after finding a treaty "selling" Mondstadt to Rex Lapis, sealed with his inimitable insignia. Historians later learned it was a forgery, made with skills Venti had honed pranking Morax. After the revolution he established the Four Winds. Vennessa founded the Knights of Favonius and ascended at Windrise, where the great oak grew; Venti draws healing from that tree.

Venti's Mavuika voice-over hints that Vennessa was Natlanese ("starting with her, I suppose the Natlanese have always been like that").

9.content: Venti covets Master Diluc's cellar and admits to pilfering food from the Dawn Winery. During the Stormterror crisis he dragged the Traveler into Angel's Share to hide from the Knights, explained the situation to Diluc in song, and won his help. Diluc interrogated the Fatui and raided their stronghold to recover the Holy Lyre, then witnessed Dvalin call Venti "Barbatos". Venti's verdict on Diluc's wine: if he won't let you sample it, at least you can enjoy the aroma.

10.content: Jean worked out Venti's identity from their dealings and had it confirmed when Dvalin named him. She helped him quietly when the Fatui tied her hands as Acting Grand Master, let him leave the Cathedral to heal at Windrise, and keeps his secret. He calls her conscientious, courageous, kind and considerate, and says she "reminds me of another good friend" without saying whom. In 5.6 she named him Windblume Star; he swapped the speech for a song, and asked whether the title came with unlimited free drinks.

11.content:
The Hexenzirkel, a circle of immensely powerful witches, once challenged the Anemo Archon. He convinced them to settle things with music instead, and they became allies. They hold tea parties he sometimes attends, and he was entrusted with the lantern to one of their meeting places. Varka, having asked Venti about it, secured a pact: the Tripartite Conference of the Knights and Church, the Anemo Archon and the Hexenzirkel, for Mondstadt's hour of need. In 5.6 Albedo invoked it; Venti called Alice on a Dodocommunication Device (accidentally reaching Varka first) and sat at the conference. Afterward he delivered the Hexenzirkel's gift to the Traveler, to be opened "when the time is right".

In 6.2 he sensed Barbeloth eavesdropping and asked her to set down her pen ("Words heard on the wind are not meant to be recorded on the page"), saying his future must remain absent from her dictionary. Her prophecy about him was "incomplete" but not "incorrect". In 6.4 Alice and the mage Nicole came to Mondstadt and built a memory bubble with his help (limited event).

12.content: Dahlia is a deacon of the Church of Favonius whom Barbatos appointed, officially and in secret, as his herald. Dahlia passes him news of the nation, and Venti answers through him, which is why Dahlia always gets "answers from Barbatos" at morning prayers. Dahlia arranged the Traveler's meeting with Venti at Starsnatch Cliff during the Durin crisis. Venti uses him as an intermediary because Dahlia "loves listening to the blustering of the wind, but crucially he has his own compass, too." Dahlia calls Venti a dear friend and the best drinker he knows. Venti allowed Dahlia and Seneschal Seamus Pegg to tell Barbara the truth; she did not believe Dahlia.

key: Song of the Dragon and Freedom
13.content: Prologue, 1.0. In the Whispering Woods, Venti was trying to heal Dvalin when the Traveler's power flared, breaking the link and poisoning Venti. He purged it at the Windrise oak. He held the Traveler aloft when Dvalin attacked the city, sang them Dvalin's story when they tracked him down, and saw that the Traveler could purify the dragon's crystallised tears. They failed to borrow the Holy Lyre legally, lost it to a Fatui thief, recovered it with Diluc and Jean, and restored it with purified tears. An Abyss Mage turned Dvalin away at Starsnatch Cliff and broke the lyre. In Act III, Venti admitted his long absences had made him the weakest Archon, dispelled the barrier on Stormterror's Lair, and empowered the Traveler to purge Dvalin in the sky above the ruins. Jean told the people the truth about Dvalin. Then Signora struck.

14.comment: Venti: Time, Istaroth and the Nameless Island
14.content: As a wind spirit, Venti met "Time" at the Thousand Winds Temple, and she entrusted him with fragments of her power and authority (told to the Traveler in Natlan, 5.8). Because of Time's help, "the first winds of freedom" blew strongly enough to free Mondstadt. Such gales suit wiping things clean rather than helping things grow, so after a few crises he made his winds gentler. In 6.2 he took the Traveler to the Nameless Island, "the place where Time and Wind met in the distant past", which Time favours because of an ode he once played there. After hearing of the Pyro Archon's clash with Ronova, the Captain's fate and the Abyss nearing Mondstadt, he said he fears a crisis beyond what humans alone can solve. "As such, I, Barbatos, will bring forth a wind strong enough to disperse whatever storm lies ahead." He used Time's residual power to hide the gale from the world, played an ode to Time with the Traveler, and afterward insisted the power was his own, like tuning an instrument. Mondstadt once worshipped Time alongside the wind, and sayings such as "Anemo brings stories while Time nurtures them" survive.

15.content: Five hundred years ago, to stop the Mare Jivari's corruption (which "is tied to time itself") from spreading beyond Tenochtzitoc, Barbatos blew it off the timeline, creating the Windless Land. The price was that some Mondstadt souls could not return home, and some merged with the local Monetoo to become the Asha. In his Story Quest (1.0) he met the old adventurer "Stanley", really Hans Archibald, who had taken the name of the partner who died saving him in the Mare Jivari. Venti revealed himself as Barbatos, called Hans by his true name, brought a breeze from the Mare Jivari and asked Hans to give him his friend's spirit, letting it rest at last. In 5.8 (Sunspray Summer Resort), with Mavuika opening a rift, he slipped into the true Mare Jivari and brought back every soul that wished to return, and restored Asha memories. Asked what he wishes for now, he said: to protect Mondstadt, and that everyone who wishes to stay there has the freedom to choose their own path.

16.content: Venti first noticed Varka as a young knight who went to the Thousand Winds Temple seeking oracles after tavern tall tales. He found only moss and an angry Ruin Guard, and laughed while batting its missiles away. Varka got his Vision thrilled that the Archon had noticed him, then got to know Barbatos and found that was not what it meant at all. He calls Barbatos carefree but serious when it counts, with good taste in drink. In 6.4 Varka sent at least ten letters home with the vice-captain Lohen, including one "for the bard in green clothes" delivered to the Thousand Winds Temple, since the Archon has no address. Venti read it, frowned, called it idle chatter between drinking buddies, and alone whispered, "Get home safe, Varka." Barbatos had earlier explained how to separate oneself from the Ley Lines; Varka still claims not to understand it. On Varka's return (limited event) they drank together, though Varka served grape juice, since Charles would never let him hear the end of it if he started drinking without him.

17.comment: Venti: Boreas, Andrius and the Wild Hunt
17.content: Andrius, Dominator of Wolves, once left Nod-Krai to contest Decarabian, then renounced his claim when the tower fell. He slept in the north for a thousand years and returned as "Boreas" with the first Knight of Boreas. When his body failed, he poured his power into the Ley Lines and became Mondstadt's North Wind. Part of his soul stayed in Nod-Krai, a feat of soul-partition rare even among gods. In 6.4 Abyss-twisted remnants of that northern half followed the Ley Lines to Wolvendom. Venti arrived strumming his lyre, asked Boreas's leave, and told the tale as song. He explained that Roland, five hundred years ago, had been "too pure of heart", vowing to wipe out all injustice in an imperfect world. He sent Dvalin to carry the Traveler and Boreas's blessed blade to Varka in Nod-Krai.

18.comment: Venti: Albedo, Durin and the Durin Crisis
18.content: Venti knows Albedo is a synthetic human made by Rhinedottir and calls such power ancient and dangerous. In Paralogism (5.6) Albedo staged his own murder trial to lure out mimics spawned from the dead dragon Durin's remains. Venti met the Traveler at Starsnatch Cliff through Dahlia and lent them a Dodocommunication Device borrowed from Alice, with the explosive removed. He was relieved the public did not learn Albedo's origin. During the monster assault he feigned helplessness before civilians, then wove wind currents for long-range communication. He detected a "child's anger" in the wind (Durin's jealousy of Rhinedottir's other child) and helped find its host. After the conference with the Hexenzirkel he sang as Albedo transmuted Mini Durin into the dragon's human successor. He later introduced the new Durin to Dvalin, sang the sleepless boy a song he loved, and in 6.2 gave him the wind to fly beside Dvalin. He also told Durin it was not his place to pry into why his mother left her story unfinished.

19.content: Venti admires that Natlan's heroes, under Mavuika, achieved "a truly god-like feat" against the Abyss, though he calls it cruel that the world made generations of humans cannon fodder. In 5.8 he holidayed in Natlan with Bennett, Mualani and Chasca, drinking everything in reach, while secretly collaborating with Mavuika on the Mare Jivari souls. The two found they shared a love of fine wine and freedom. She invited him to the tribes' rowdy banquets and he proposed a joint Mondstadt-Natlan banquet someday. Wiki summaries say he also befriended an earlier Pyro Archon, but canon gives few details. His voice-over jokingly quotes old epics calling the Pyro Archon "a wayward, warmongering wretch".

20.content: Ei: Venti remembers her as Makoto's kagemusha, perfecting her martial skill, and whispers that her weakness is desserts. Ei says she sensed from their first meeting they would not get along, and that he drinks a lot. Nahida: he says her dreams are like his ballads, "full of emotion and imagination", and that they get along well. Furina: he wants to invite her to perform at the Windblume Festival and would not be surprised if she had saved the whole world. In the 6.4 limited event he said the Traveler did right in Inazuma and that it had pained him to see the nation as it was.

21.content: Once, after a night of fighting, Xiao collapsed under his karmic debt. A clear flute melody came over the mountains on the wind and played until dawn, easing his pain. He did not chase the player, but he reasoned only one of The Seven could help him. Venti appears as the flute player in the official Yakshas teaser. Xiao knows "Venti" is the name Barbatos uses, and cuts himself off when asked about his tunes.

22.comment: Venti: Homeward, He Who Caught the Wind (6.4 event)
22.content: During a limited-time 6.4 event, Alice and the mage Nicole built a "memory bubble" in which the Traveler relived their first days in Mondstadt, with Venti and Dvalin waiting in the Whispering Woods as before. Varka joined the replay. When the Abyss corrupted the bubble into a version where the Traveler never came, the group had to defeat a fully corrupted Dvalin. Venti said he could have handled the real crisis alone, "but it wouldn't have gone quite so well." At the banquet afterward, seated with Varka on the hands of the Anemo Archon Statue, he talked about the Gnoses, Signora and Snezhnaya, and was crestfallen when Varka handed him grape juice.

23.comment: Venti: Venti at festivals and events
23.content: Limited-time event appearances, canon but not universally known: Invitation of Windblume (1.4), where he taught a love-poem class and explained the Windblume's meaning atop Decarabian's tower. Midsummer Island Adventure (1.6), where he had Dvalin fly Klee's party to the Golden Apple Archipelago and asked them to keep it secret. Hues of the Violet Garden (2.6), where Kamisato Ayato invited him to Inazuma, Kujou Sara arrested him passed out drunk for illegal entry until his invitation turned up in his hat, and Albedo used him as a painting model. Of Ballads and Brews (3.1): at Weinlesefest he suggested Razor brew his parents' wine and used "far-flung winds" to accept the Archon's offerings without exposing himself. The Exquisite Night Chimes (3.4): Lantern Rite in Liyue, pretending not to know Zhongli. Windblume's Breath (3.5): he hinted at the Hexenzirkel's lantern prophecy.
